subtype: Approach: switching tactics after a bad practice score [Revision]
passage: Lavanya sat on the string cot outside her house in the village and made a quiz for herself, ten questions from her science chapter. She had read it twice. She scored five out of ten. She looked at the paper for a while. "Reading is not working," she said quietly. That evening her brother Ramesh saw her cutting a notebook page into small cards. On each she wrote a point on one side and a question on the other. She shuffled and tested herself. The next night she quizzed herself again and got eight right.

qa.q: What score did Lavanya get on her first quiz?
qa.a: She scored five out of ten.

qa.q: How did Lavanya feel after looking at her score of five out of ten?
qa.a: She was disappointed but clear-headed. She quietly said reading was not working, which led her to change her method.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Lavanya add to her cards, and why?
qa.a: She could ask Ramesh to read her the questions. Answering out loud to someone else helps her practise saying it.

qa.q: How might Ramesh see Lavanya cutting the notebook page into cards?
qa.a: Ramesh sees his sister trying something new after a poor score, and he may be curious or proud. He notices her working hard on her own.

grounding: After scoring five out of ten on her own quiz, a girl notices reading alone is not working and switches to key-point cards she uses to quiz herself, and her next score rises.
